title: The Open-Air Rest Cure
paras: In the late nineteenth century, a distinctive daily routine developed in European mountain sanatoriums. Patients with tuberculosis followed a [[sequence|sequence]] of meals, temperature checks and long periods of rest outdoors. Before effective medicines existed, doctors hoped that fresh air, sunlight and regular food would [[ease|ease]] symptoms and help weakened bodies recover.

The buildings reflected this belief. Long, [[airy|airy]] balconies allowed beds to be wheeled outside, while roofs protected patients from rain. Wealthier guests might enjoy [[luxurious|luxurious]] private rooms, but simpler institutions used shared sleeping areas. These were not necessarily considered [[inferior|inferior]]: access to outdoor air mattered more than expensive furniture. Institutions also had to [[recruit|recruit]] nurses willing to manage blankets, meals and patients through cold winters.

To picture the boredom of prolonged rest, imagine a fictional patient, Anna. Beside her bed stands a small [[walnut|walnut]] table with an illustrated book about [[extinct|extinct]] animals. She has read it twice, but opens it again while waiting for lunch. One common [[guideline|guideline]] in sanatoriums was to avoid unnecessary physical effort, although details varied between institutions. In this imagined scene, Anna dislikes resting but follows the rule [[anyhow|anyhow]], hoping to recover.

By the middle of the twentieth century, effective antibiotics had transformed tuberculosis treatment. The balcony cure gradually lost its central medical role, and many sanatoriums closed or found new uses.
zh: 19世纪末，欧洲山区的结核病疗养院形成了一套独特的日常作息。结核病患者按顺序进餐、测量体温，并长时间在户外静卧。在有效药物问世之前，医生希望新鲜空气、阳光和规律饮食能够缓解症状，帮助虚弱的身体恢复。
建筑也体现了这种观念。宽敞通风的长阳台方便人们将病床推出室外，屋顶则为患者遮雨。富裕的住客或许能享用豪华的单人房，而条件简朴的机构则采用多人寝室。这些设施不一定被认为较差：能接触室外空气比昂贵的家具更重要。疗养院还得招募愿意在寒冬里照料患者、安排饮食并管理被褥的护士。
要体会长时间静养的乏味，不妨想象一位虚构的患者安娜。她的床旁放着一张核桃木小桌，桌上有一本介绍已灭绝动物的图画书。她已经读过两遍，却在等待午餐时又翻开了它。疗养院的一项常见指导原则是避免不必要的体力消耗，不过各机构的具体规定有所不同。在这个想象的场景中，安娜不喜欢静养，却仍然遵守规定，希望能够康复。
到20世纪中叶，有效的抗生素已经改变了结核病的治疗方式。阳台静养逐渐失去了在医疗中的核心地位，许多疗养院关闭或改作其他用途。

q.s: The outdoor resting routine emerged before effective tuberculosis medicines were available.
q.why: 首段指出该作息形成于有效药物问世前。

q.s: Expensive furnishings were regarded as more important than access to fresh air.
q.why: 第二段指出室外空气比昂贵家具更重要。

q.s: Most former sanatoriums were converted into hotels.
q.why: 末段仅说改作其他用途，未说明具体用途。
